subject: Replacement risk: performance mapping + term proposal
messages:
From: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@lumenstore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Concern: bakeoff with NimbusAI + capacity ask

Marissa,

Quick note — our engineering team is pushing for a guided bakeoff with NimbusAI next week. They came in with a perf claim that would reduce our per-query latency by ~30% on our 99th percentile tests, and the procurement team is getting nervous about our current pricing/term profile.

We also have a Q3 traffic forecast spike that will require roughly 2.4x more reserved capacity if we keep current batching patterns. Before we go deep with a competitor, can you map Redwood's current performance envelope against their claim and share any program-level term concessions you can offer (short of an SOS-level credit)? Procurement is asking for firm numbers by Friday.

Cc: procurement@lumenstore.com

Thanks,
Andrew Hayes
CTO, LumenStore
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@lumenstore.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Concern: bakeoff with NimbusAI + capacity ask

Andrew — thanks for the heads up and totally understand the urgency. We don't want you chasing false promises in a bakeoff. Proposed next steps: 

1) Quick perf baseline run on a representative subset of your traffic (we can run within 48 hours). Markus, can engineering scope that and flag any feature parity gaps?
2) We will produce a short benchmark report (99/95/median) and an ops cost delta with and without prefix/KV caching engaged.
3) On terms: we can present a targeted Q3 burst plan (2.4x) with a one-time capacity guarantee and a conditional discount for commit + accelerated ramp if you lock for 12 months. Draft terms attached (redwood-term-proposal-v2.pdf) and a compact perf summary csv that Markus can expand.

If Friday is the procurement deadline, we should schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow morning to demo the baseline scope and agree inputs. Available windows: 9:30–10:00am or 11:00–11:30am PT.

Attachments: lumenstore-q4-perf-summary.csv; redwood-term-proposal-v2.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: prep for LumenStore baseline

Team — short internal thread to align before the customer sync.

Markus: please validate the sample size and make sure we include cold-start and KV-cache-on baselines. If Nimbus is using a different tokenization/segment size we should call that out.
Monica: CS should prepare an ops runbook for the 2.4x burst scenario (scaling plan, SLA considerations). Also confirm what support hours/customer success guardrails we can attach to the conditional discount.
Marissa: If we offer a 12-month commit + 10% overage credit backstop, is that acceptable to legal/pricing? I can draft a one-pager.

I'll standby for your notes — want to go tight into the customer call.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@lumenstore.com>, procurement@lumenstore.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: benchmark plan, capacity guarantee, and term adjustments

Andrew — following our internal scoping, please find a concise proposal: 

• Benchmark plan: Redwood will run a customer-representative baseline within 48 hours and deliver a short report with 99/95/median latency and throughput at your target QPS. We'll include KV cache on/off and cold-start windows. (See attached lumenstore-q4-perf-summary.csv for initial sample).

• Capacity guarantee: Redwood will reserve the requested Q3 burst capacity (2.4x) on a temporary guaranteed pool for the quarter to match your projected peak. If actual usage stays above the guaranteed pool for >10 days we will trigger an automatic temporary scale event.

• Commercial terms: 12-month committed term, with a launch-quarter discount structure. We can front a 6% onboarding credit against the first invoice and add a conditional 8% overage credit if commit is signed within 10 business days. Full pricing grid attached (redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx) and summary in the attached PDF (redwood-term-proposal-v2.pdf).

• Next step: proposed bakeoff window Tue 2/16–2/18. We'll run parallel runs and publish a single comparison doc. If Redwood meets parity on 99th latency within a 10% margin, we will commit to the commercial terms above and a rolling rollout plan.

If that looks reasonable I'll get legal to prepare the short-form amendment. Happy to join a procurement call if you want Mark (procurement) on.
